memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine follow‑up for hypothyroidism and general health review.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27.0 (obese). Pulse regular, no edema, thyroid not enlarged.
IMPRESSION: 1. Hypothyroidism, currently on levothyroxine 50 mcg OD, TSH borderline high. 2. Overweight per Asian cut‑offs. Advise diet and activity. 3. Age‑appropriate screening: fasting lipid profile and fasting glucose ordered.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue levothyroxine 50 mcg OD. Return if fatigue worsens, weight gain, palpitations, or any new chest pain.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
TSH 4.8 mIU/L (0.5‑4.5) – slightly high.
Free T4 11.2 pmol/L (9.0‑19.0) – normal.
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 3.0 mmol/L (<2.6) – borderline high, HDL 1.2 mmol/L (>1.0), Triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (<1.7) – borderline high.
Fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5) – mildly elevated.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Review of thyroid medication; patient reports mild fatigue and weight gain of 2 kg.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/86 mmHg, weight 80 kg, BMI 27.6 (obese). No goiter, skin dry.
IMPRESSION: Hypothyroidism with inadequate control (TSH rising). Increase levothyroxine. Continue lifestyle advice for obesity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase levothyroxine to 75 mcg OD. Return if palpitations, tremor, excessive sweating, or worsening fatigue.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
TSH 3.2 mIU/L (0.5‑4.5) – within target.
Free T4 12.5 pmol/L (9.0‑19.0) – normal.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine check; patient feels better, no fatigue, weight stable.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 79.5 kg, BMI 27.5 (obese). No thyroid enlargement.
IMPRESSION: Hypothyroidism well‑controlled on current dose. Overweight persists – reinforce diet and activity. Annual lipid and glucose check due.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase levothyroxine to 100 mcg OD to ensure adequate replacement given age‑related changes. Return if weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, or chest discomfort.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.0 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.8 mmol/L (<2.6) – slightly high, HDL 1.3 mmol/L (>1.0), Triglycerides 1.6 mmol/L (<1.7).
Fasting glucose 5.4 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5) – normal.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Resting ECG: Sinus rhythm, rate 72 bpm. No ST‑segment changes, no Q waves. Left ventricular voltage within normal limits. No arrhythmias.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Endocrinology, Vikram Hospital, for optimisation of thyroid replacement in elderly patient with borderline lipids and persistent overweight. Request TSH, free T4, thyroid antibodies, and advice on levothyroxine dosing.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Endocrinology report: TSH 2.9 mIU/L, free T4 13.0 pmol/L, TPO antibodies negative. Advise to maintain levothyroxine 100 mcg OD, monitor TSH in 6‑8 weeks. Lifestyle modification for weight; consider metformin only if diabetes develops.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling a bit more tired over the past week and noticed my weight creeping up again despite walking.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Fatigue and slight weight gain reported by patient.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 81.0 kg, BMI 28.0 (obese). No thyroid enlargement, skin mild dryness.
IMPRESSION: Possible slight under‑replacement of levothyroxine; TSH to check. Reinforce weight‑management advice.
ARRANGEMENTS: Order TSH and free T4. Continue levothyroxine 100 mcg OD. Return if worsening fatigue, palpitations, heat intolerance, or new chest pain.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
TSH 2.7 mIU/L (0.5‑4.5) – within target.
Free T4 13.2 pmol/L (9.0‑19.0) – normal.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2026-07-20 at 10:30 AM with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine review; patient reports feeling well, no fatigue, weight stable at 80.5 kg.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 80.5 kg, BMI 27.9 (obese). No goiter, skin normal.
IMPRESSION: Hypothyroidism adequately controlled on levothyroxine 100 mcg OD. Overweight persists – continue diet and activity counsel. No further labs needed until next annual screen.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue levothyroxine 100 mcg OD. Return if weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, chest pain, breathlessness, or fever >39°C.
